posts.title: What is Namaste Salesforce?
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Namaste Salesforce is a free, community-driven learning platform for the Salesforce ecosystem. Whether you are a complete beginner, a working admin moving toward development, or an architect going deep on integration and scale, you'll find structured content built for your level.

Everything here is organised into four kinds of content:

  • Courses — self-contained, project-based learning that takes you from zero to a working skill.
  • Roadmaps — ordered learning paths that string courses and lessons together role by role.
  • Documentation — the help center you're reading now: how-tos, references and answers.
  • Blog — shorter articles, tips and release commentary from the ecosystem.
Tip: You don't need a Salesforce org to start. Most foundational lessons run entirely in the browser.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: A free, open learning platform for the Salesforce ecosystem — courses, roadmaps, docs and a blog.

posts.title: Create your free account
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Creating an account is free and takes less than a minute. An account lets you save your place in a course, track roadmap progress across visits, and unlock member-only lessons.

How to sign up

  1. Click Sign in in the top navigation, then choose Sign up.
  2. Enter your name and email address.
  3. Check your inbox for a magic sign-in link — there's no password to remember.
  4. Click the link and you're in.
Tip: We use passwordless sign-in. If a link expires, just request a new one from the same screen.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Sign up in under a minute to save progress, unlock member lessons and track your roadmaps.

posts.title: Navigating the site
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

The top navigation is the fastest way around the site. From left to right you'll find the logo (home), a Topics menu that opens a tag cloud, the main sections, search, and your account menu.

  • Topics — hover the menu next to the logo to jump to any subject area.
  • Search — open it from the navbar to filter courses, lessons and docs as you type.
  • Dark mode — toggle the sun/moon icon; your choice is remembered on this device.
  • Account — sign in to see your avatar, saved progress and the Become an Author link.
Tip: On mobile, the menu collapses behind the hamburger icon; lesson pages show a left-hand drawer for the curriculum.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Find your way around the top navigation, topic menu, search and dark mode.

posts.title: Free vs member content
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Most of Namaste Salesforce is free forever. A small amount of content is reserved for signed-in members to support the project.

  • Free, no account — browsing courses, roadmaps, docs and the blog; most foundational lessons.
  • Free account — saving progress, unlocking member lessons, and following roadmaps across visits.
  • Member — a handful of advanced, in-depth lessons marked with a lock icon.

A lock icon on a lesson means it needs a member account. A Preview badge means you can watch part of it before signing in.

"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: What's free forever, what needs an account, and what's reserved for members.

posts.title: Choosing your first course
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

If you're new, the hardest part is knowing where to start. Use this quick guide:

  • Brand new to Salesforce → start with the Admin Fundamentals course or the Admin roadmap.
  • Comfortable as an admin, want to code → try the Apex course.
  • Building UIs → the Lightning Web Components course.
  • Interested in AI → look for Agentforce and Einstein content.
Tip: Every course page lists its level, estimated time and what you'll build, so you can judge fit before starting.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Not sure where to begin? Pick a starting point based on your goal and experience.

posts.title: Update your profile
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Your profile controls how you appear across the site — for example, as an author byline if you contribute content.

  1. Open your account menu (avatar, top right) and choose Account settings.
  2. Edit your name, bio and social links.
  3. Upload a profile photo — a square image works best.
  4. Save. Changes appear immediately.
Tip: A profile photo also shows up next to your lessons in course curriculums when you're the author.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Change your display name, bio and profile photo.

posts.title: Change your email address
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Because sign-in is passwordless, there's no password to change — you sign in with a magic link sent to your email. To move to a new address:

  1. Go to Account settings.
  2. Update the email field to your new address.
  3. Confirm from the verification link sent to the new inbox.
Tip: If you've lost access to your old inbox and can't sign in, contact support and we'll help you recover the account.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Move your account to a new email safely.

posts.title: Manage email notifications
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

You're in full control of what lands in your inbox.

  • Open Account settings → Email preferences.
  • Toggle newsletters, new-course announcements and comment replies independently.
  • Every email also has an unsubscribe link at the foot.
Tip: Turning off newsletters won't affect essential account emails like sign-in links.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Control which emails you receive — new courses, newsletters and replies.

posts.title: Profile privacy
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

By default your learning activity is private. Only the information you choose to publish is visible to others.

  • Public — your name, bio and photo, but only if you're a published author.
  • Private — your email, progress, enrolled courses and roadmap status.

If you never contribute content, your profile is effectively invisible to other learners.

"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: What's public on your profile and what stays private.

posts.title: Delete your account
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

You can delete your account at any time. This is permanent and removes your progress, saved courses and profile.

  1. Go to Account settings.
  2. Scroll to Delete account at the bottom.
  3. Confirm. Active members should cancel their subscription first.
Tip: Deleting your account cancels any active membership. Published articles may be anonymised rather than removed.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: How to permanently remove your account and data.

posts.title: How courses work
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

A course is a self-contained learning unit made of ordered lessons. Each course page opens with an overview — what you'll build, the level, and estimated time — followed by the full curriculum.

  • Lessons are grouped and play in sequence.
  • Some lessons are video, some are written articles — both count toward progress.
  • A lock icon marks member-only lessons; a preview badge means you can sample it.
Tip: Use the curriculum sidebar (or the left drawer on mobile) to jump between lessons at any time.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: The structure of a course: lessons, sections, progress and resources.

posts.title: Enrolling in a course
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Free courses have no enrollment step. Open any course and click Start learning (or any lesson) to begin. If you're signed in, your progress saves automatically.

\n

For member courses, you'll be prompted to sign in or upgrade when you reach a locked lesson. Everything before the lock is still free to explore.

"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: There's no checkout for free courses — just start learning.

posts.title: Tracking your progress
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

When you're signed in, the site remembers which lessons you've opened and how far you are in each course and roadmap.

  • Progress is tied to your account, so it follows you across devices.
  • The curriculum highlights your current lesson.
  • Roadmaps show how far along each track you are.
Tip: Not signed in? Progress is only kept for your current browser session. Create a free account to keep it for good.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: How progress is saved and where to see it.

posts.title: Video vs article lessons
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Lessons come in two formats, marked with an icon on the curriculum:

  • Video — a recorded walkthrough with a player and, often, a written summary below.
  • Article — a written lesson with code blocks, screenshots and callouts.

Both formats are treated equally for progress, and many lessons combine a video with written notes so you can follow along in whichever way works for you.

"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Both formats count — pick what suits how you learn.

posts.title: Downloading lesson resources
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Many lessons include downloadable resources \u2014 sample code, slides, or a PDF cheat-sheet. When available, they appear in a Resources block within the lesson body.

\n
Tip: Code samples are usually linked to a public repository so you can clone the whole project at once.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Where to find sample code, slides and cheat-sheets.

posts.title: Marking lessons complete
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Opening a lesson marks it as visited. As you move through a course with Next, each lesson is recorded so the curriculum shows what's done and what's left.

\n

To revisit, just click any earlier lesson \u2014 nothing is locked once you've reached it. Your furthest point is always remembered.

"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: How completion works and how to reset it.

posts.title: What are roadmaps?
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Roadmaps (also called training tracks) are curated, ordered learning paths. Where a course teaches one skill, a roadmap strings many lessons together into a journey — for example, everything you need to go from beginner to job-ready admin.

  • Each roadmap is divided into sections (stages of the journey).
  • Each section contains several modules you complete in order.
  • Prev / Next flows across section boundaries, so you never lose your place.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Ordered, role-based paths that connect courses and lessons end to end.

posts.title: Following a roadmap
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Open a roadmap and click Start learning to begin at the first module. From there, the Next button carries you through every module and across every section automatically.

\n
Tip: The curriculum sidebar groups modules by section so you can always see the bigger picture and jump ahead.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Start at the top and let Next carry you through every section.

posts.title: Roadmap sections explained
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Long paths are easier to follow in stages. Each roadmap section represents a milestone \u2014 for example Foundations, then Core Skills, then Going Further.

\n

Sections are ordered, and within each section modules play in sequence. When you finish the last module of a section, Next moves you into the first module of the following section.

"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Why roadmaps are split into sections and how they're ordered.

posts.title: Switching between roadmaps
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

You're not locked into a single roadmap. Your progress is tracked independently for each one, so you can follow the Admin roadmap and dip into the Developer roadmap without losing your place in either.

\n
Tip: Head to the Roadmaps page any time to see all available tracks and pick up where you left off.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: You can follow more than one path at a time.

posts.title: Recommended paths by role
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Not sure which roadmap fits? Use your target role:

  • Want to run a Salesforce org → Admin roadmap.
  • Want to write code and build apps → Developer roadmap.
  • Want to work with data and analytics → Data & Analytics roadmap.
Tip: You can always switch later — roadmaps overlap, and skills carry across.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Which roadmap to pick based on where you want to go.

posts.title: Free vs Pro membership
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Namaste Salesforce is free at its core. A Pro membership unlocks a small set of advanced lessons and supports the project so we can keep building.

  • Free — all courses' overviews, most lessons, roadmaps, docs and the blog.
  • Pro — every member-locked lesson, plus early access to new content.
Tip: You never need Pro to learn the fundamentals — it's for going deeper on advanced topics.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: What each tier includes so you can decide if Pro is worth it.

posts.title: Upgrade to Pro
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Ready to unlock member content? You can upgrade in a couple of steps:

  1. Sign in to your account.
  2. Open the account menu and choose Upgrade (or hit any locked lesson).
  3. Pick a plan and enter your payment details.
  4. You're upgraded instantly — locked lessons unlock right away.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: How to become a member and unlock everything.

posts.title: Manage your subscription
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Manage everything about your membership from Account settings → Billing:

  • See your current plan and next billing date.
  • Switch between monthly and annual billing.
  • Update the card on file.
  • Download past invoices.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: View, change or update your plan and billing details.

posts.title: Payment methods
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Payments are handled securely by our payment provider. We accept major credit and debit cards. Your card details are never stored on our servers.

\n
Tip: Seeing a card declined? Check with your bank first \u2014 international transactions are sometimes blocked by default.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Which cards and payment options we accept.

posts.title: Refund policy
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

If Pro isn't what you expected, contact support within 14 days of your first payment and we'll issue a full refund \u2014 no lengthy questions.

\n

Refunds apply to the most recent payment. After a refund, your account returns to the free tier and locked lessons re-lock.

"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Our approach to refunds if Pro isn't right for you.

posts.title: Cancel your membership
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

You can cancel any time and keep your free account and all your progress.

  1. Go to Account settings → Billing.
  2. Click Cancel subscription.
  3. You keep Pro access until the end of the paid period, then return to free.
Tip: Cancelling doesn't delete your account or progress — only future payments stop.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Stop future billing while keeping your account.

posts.title: Do you offer certificates?
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Yes \u2014 when you complete a course or roadmap, you earn a certificate of completion you can share. Note these are recognition of finishing our content, not official Salesforce certifications.

\n
Tip: For official credentials, use these courses to prepare, then sit the exam on Salesforce's own certification platform.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: What completion recognition is available today.

posts.title: Getting your certificate of completion
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Once you've completed every lesson in a course (or every module in a roadmap), a Claim certificate option appears on the overview page.

  1. Finish all lessons — the curriculum shows 100%.
  2. Open the course or roadmap overview.
  3. Click Claim certificate and download the PDF.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: How to claim and download your certificate.

posts.title: Sharing your achievements
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Certificates include a shareable link and are sized for LinkedIn. Add them to the Licenses & certifications section of your profile, or share the link anywhere.

\n
Tip: Tag us when you share \u2014 we love celebrating learner milestones.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Post your progress to LinkedIn and beyond.

posts.title: My progress isn't saving
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

If progress isn't sticking, work through these in order:

  1. Make sure you're signed in — progress only persists for logged-in accounts.
  2. Check you're using the same account (and email) across devices.
  3. Disable private/incognito mode, which can block saved state.
  4. Allow cookies for the site.
Tip: Still stuck? Contact support with the course name and we'll investigate.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Fixes when your completion or place isn't being remembered.

posts.title: Who can contribute?
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Namaste Salesforce is community-maintained. You don't need to be a certified expert to contribute — clear, accurate, helpful content matters more than titles.

  • Admins sharing real-world configuration tips.
  • Developers writing lessons on Apex, LWC or integration.
  • Anyone spotting and fixing gaps or errors in existing docs.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Anyone with Salesforce knowledge and a willingness to teach.

posts.title: Apply to become an author
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Ready to contribute? Start here:

  1. Sign in, then open the Become an Author link in your account menu.
  2. Tell us what you'd like to write and your relevant experience.
  3. We'll grant contributor access and walk you through the tools.
Tip: New authors are paired with an editor for their first piece.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: The quick path from learner to contributor.

posts.title: Author guidelines
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Great lessons share a few traits. Aim for:

  • One clear objective per lesson — what the reader can do afterwards.
  • Working, tested code and accurate steps.
  • Screenshots or short clips where they clarify.
  • Plain language over jargon; define terms on first use.
Tip: When in doubt, teach it the way you'd have wanted to learn it.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: The style and quality bar we hold content to.

posts.title: Submitting your content
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Contributors write drafts in the editor and submit them for review. Add the right tags (course or section, level, type) so the theme renders your lesson correctly, then submit.

\n

An editor reviews for accuracy and style, suggests changes, and schedules publication once it's ready.

"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: How drafts move from your editor to publication.

posts.title: The editorial process
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Every submission goes through a light editorial pass so learners can trust the content:

  1. Technical review — is it accurate and does the code work?
  2. Editorial review — clarity, structure and consistency.
  3. Tagging & placement — the right course, section and level.
  4. Publish — your byline goes live with the lesson.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: What happens between submitting and going live.

posts.title: Join the community
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Learning is easier together. Join the community to ask questions, share what you're building, and get unstuck faster.

  • Ask and answer questions with other learners.
  • Share projects and certificates.
  • Hear about new courses and roadmaps first.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Where learners and authors talk, help each other and share wins.

posts.title: Report a bug
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

If something on the site isn't working — a broken link, a video that won't load, a rendering glitch — let us know so we can fix it.

  1. Note the page URL and what you expected to happen.
  2. Open an issue on our GitHub repository, or use the contact form.
  3. Include your browser and device if it's a display problem.
Tip: Screenshots help enormously — attach one if you can.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Found something broken? Here's how to tell us.

posts.title: Request a topic
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

We add new courses and roadmaps every month, and learner requests shape the queue. If there's a topic you want covered, tell us.

\n

Use the Request a topic button on the Roadmaps page, or the contact form. Popular requests move up the list.

"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Tell us what to build next.

posts.title: Code of conduct
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Everyone is welcome here, whatever their level. To keep it that way, we ask that you:

  • Be respectful and assume good intent.
  • Keep answers constructive — we all started somewhere.
  • No spam, self-promotion or harassment.
Tip: Reports are handled confidentially. Serious violations lead to removal.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: The simple rules that keep the community welcoming.

posts.title: Contact support
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Can't find your answer in the help center? Reach out and a real person will help.

  • Use the contact form for account, billing or technical issues.
  • For content errors, open a GitHub issue so it's tracked in the open.
  • Include your account email (never your password) so we can find you.
Tip: We aim to reply within two business days.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: How to reach a human when you need one.

posts.title: I can't sign in
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Sign-in is passwordless — you request a link and click it. If it's not working:

  1. Check the link hasn't expired (they're single-use and time-limited) — request a fresh one.
  2. Look in spam/promotions folders for the email.
  3. Make sure you're opening the link on the same device/browser where possible.
  4. Add our sending address to your contacts to stop future links being filtered.
Tip: Still locked out? Contact support and we'll verify your identity another way.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Fixes for magic-link and login problems.

posts.title: A video won't play
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

If a video won't start or keeps buffering:

  • Check your internet connection and try lowering quality.
  • Disable ad-blockers or privacy extensions for this site — they can block players.
  • Try a different browser to rule out an extension.
  • Member videos require you to be signed in with an active membership.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Common causes when a lesson video is stuck.

posts.title: Dark mode isn't working
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

The site remembers your light/dark choice per device. If it's stuck:

  1. Click the sun/moon toggle in the navbar to switch manually.
  2. If it won't stick, allow cookies/local storage for the site.
  3. Clearing site data resets it to follow your system setting.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: How the theme toggle works and how to reset it.

posts.title: Search isn't finding what I expect
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

Search filters courses, lessons and docs by title as you type. If you're not seeing a result:

  • Try fewer or more general keywords.
  • Check spelling — search matches titles closely.
  • Some member content only appears once you're signed in.
"}], "direction": null, "format": "", "indent": 0, "type": "root", "version": 1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Tips to get better search results.

posts.title: Clearing your cache
posts.lexical:
{"root": {"children": [{"type": "html", "version": 1, "html": "

If the site looks broken after an update — missing styles, old content — a stale cache is often the cause.

  1. Do a hard refresh (Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + R).
  2. If that doesn't help, clear the site's cached files in your browser settings.
  3. Reload the page.
